Surveys of the American pika in five park units of the western United States

Source: R/data.R
pika.Rd

Sign of the American pika (Ochotona princeps) recorded on repeated surveys of 771 plots in five park units of Oregon, Idaho and California, from 2010 to 2021, with no surveys in 2015 and 2016. Plots are circles of 12 m radius, searched for up to 30 minutes. Fresh scat, fresh haypiles and calls can be false, whereas sightings and some fresh scat are unambiguous, so the data fit a false-positive occupancy model with a verified method.

Usage

pika

Format

A data frame with 5,126 rows, one per survey, and 29 columns:

plot, Plot_ID

Plot, with and without the park code.

Park

Park unit: Crater Lake (CRLA), Craters of the Moon (CRMO), Lava Beds (LABE), Lassen Volcanic (LAVO) or Newberry (NEWB, from 2017).

Survey_ID, Location_ID

Survey, and plot-year (4,012 values).

Field_Date, Year, Month, Yday

Date of the survey (day/month/year, as text), and its year, month and day of the year.

Season, ssn

Season of the survey, as text (summer, or autumm as spelled in the source) and as 0 or 1. The source describes ssn as the original survey (summer) or the resurvey (autumn), but 2,489 surveys are in autumn and 1,107 are resurveys by resurv.

FS, OS, FH, OH

Number of fresh and old scat and fresh and old haypile observations.

PC, PS

Number of calls and sightings.

FS_U

Number of fresh scat observations classed as unambiguous. See Details.

hassign

1 if the survey recorded any of the six signs above.

resurv

1 for a resurvey, 0 for the original survey. These 1,107 are the second surveys of a plot-year; the seven third surveys have 0.

PerClass_Rock, PerClass_Bare, PerClass_Grass, PerClass_Shrub, PerClass_Tree, PerClass_Forb

Cover class of rock, bare ground, grasses, shrubs, trees and forbs, as text. Goldman et al. (2023) give the method, but not the limits of each class or the meaning of T.

lava_complx

Rock complexity, 1 to 3. Goldman et al. (2023) give the levels as low, intermediate and high. It is missing on all surveys at Lassen Volcanic and on 294 others, although a note to their Table 1 names Lava Beds.

tmaxmean

Mean daily maximum summer temperature (°C), from gridMET.

dailysumppt

Sum of daily precipitation over the previous water year (mm), from gridMET.

Source

Goldman, M. R., Shinderman, M., Jeffress, M. R., Rodhouse, T. J., & Shoemaker, K. T. (2023). Data from: Integrating multiple sign types to improve occupancy estimation for inconspicuous species. Dryad. doi:10.5061/dryad.ttdz08m2n . Licence CC0. Data collected by the OSU Cascades Human and Ecosystem Resilience and Sustainability Lab with support from the National Park Service; uses of them should attribute that source.

Details

Rows and columns are those of post_process.csv in the public deposit, with empty cells, which the source defines as no data available, as NA. The script is data-raw/pika.R in the package repository.

Fresh scat is unambiguous when the surveyor's notes describe fresh mucous holding it together, or when a fresh haypile was seen on the same survey (Goldman et al., 2023). Those notes were kept consistently only in 2019 to 2021. FS_U is NA on 682 surveys, all from 2010 to 2018, all with fresh scat and none with a fresh haypile. vignette("dynamic") treats these NA as 0, so the scat of those surveys is ambiguous.

A verified method built from FS_U is not independent of the automated occasions of the same survey. Every survey with both fresh scat and a fresh haypile has FS_U above 0, so a haypile can turn scat into a verified detection. The rule also differs between years, because of the notes.

References

Goldman, M. R., Shinderman, M., Jeffress, M. R., Rodhouse, T. J., & Shoemaker, K. T. (2023). Integrating multiple sign types to improve occupancy estimation for inconspicuous species. Ecology and Evolution, 13, e10019. doi:10.1002/ece3.10019

See also

vignette("dynamic") fits fp_occu_dyn() to these data.

Examples

table(pika$Park, pika$Year)
#>       
#>        2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021
#>   CRLA  135  138  171  141  130    0  123  128    0   95
#>   CRMO  106  170  176  122  132  119  129  121  130  130
#>   LABE  151  101  130  114  150  126  130  130   89   68
#>   LAVO  117  143   75  124  123  128  129  127   49    0
#>   NEWB    0    0    0    0    0  130  133  133    0  130

# one automated occasion per ambiguous sign, and sightings and unambiguous
# fresh scat as the verified occasion, with years as seasons
u <- ifelse(is.na(pika$FS_U), 0, pika$FS_U)
year <- factor(pika$Year, levels = 2010:2021)
sign <- function(name, y) {
  data.frame(site = pika$plot, sign = name, y = as.integer(y), year = year)
}
auto <- rbind(sign("scat", pika$FS > 0 & u == 0), sign("haypile", pika$FH > 0),
              sign("call", pika$PC > 0))
verified <- data.frame(site = pika$plot, y = as.integer(pika$PS > 0 | u > 0),
                       year = year)
plots <- unique(pika[c("plot", "Park")])
d <- fp_data(auto, data.frame(site = plots$plot, park = plots$Park), verified,
             season = "year")
#> Warning: Automated effort is very unequal among sites (3 to 57 occasions); check that occasions were not lost or duplicated.
#> Warning: 2 season(s) have no data at any site (e.g. 2015, 2016); they enter only through the transitions of occupancy.
